reason: The current Python tick owns sequencing, state replacement, metadata copying, invariant checks, routing, flow and agent lifecycle.
The current Rust extension exposes isolated Vec-in/Vec-out kernels and the Python adapter converts NumPy arrays through Python lists on each call.
A whole-engine ownership boundary removes recurrent allocation, Python object traversal and per-stage FFI crossings that hotspot-only migration cannot eliminate.
The existing Python implementation remains a frozen scientific oracle until the Rust engine passes full shadow parity.
not_a_claim: This audit does not claim a measured speedup.
It does not authorize a Rust default before the terminal promotion PR.
It does not authorize GPU mutation of canonical state without a separate admission gate.

rust_engine: routing graph, dynamic potentials, candidate caches and reroute
active-agent allocation, movement, completion and failure
invariant checks, replay digest, checkpoint and restore
runtime metrics required for scientific validation
optional_device_kernels: dense flow/turn arithmetic with persistent device state
no graph-search or branch-heavy event authority unless separately demonstrated

crates.name: metroflow-core
crates.role: pure Rust engine; no Python dependency

crates.name: metroflow-python
crates.role: thin PyO3 facade and NumPy snapshot bridge

compatibility.rule: Keep as a compatibility facade until the coarse Engine API is accepted; do not delete the Python oracle before final promotion.

forbidden_default_path: Vec<Vec<T>> crossing the Python boundary for runtime batches
silent fallback from Rust to Python or GPU
Python and Rust both mutating canonical state in one tick
ffi_contract.gil: Long-running step/chunk execution must release the GIL; snapshot construction may reacquire it.
ffi_contract.snapshot_rule: Copy or borrow only at declared observation/checkpoint boundaries, never as an implicit per-tick side effect.

data_layout.static_graph: dense index space plus stable external IDs; CSR adjacency and turn tables
data_layout.dynamic: structure-of-arrays with fixed dtypes and explicit units
data_layout.ragged: offsets plus flat values; no nested vectors at FFI
data_layout.masks: byte/bit masks selected by measured cost; canonical serialization fixed
data_layout.index_width: u32/i32 only where bounded mechanically; otherwise u64/usize with checked conversion

float_policy.authority: preserve current field-specific f32/f64 semantics until an explicit parity PR changes them
float_policy.reductions: fixed partition and deterministic serial combine for floating reductions
float_policy.no_fast_math: forbidden before a dedicated drift contract

rayon.pool: engine-owned ThreadPool with explicit thread count; do not use an uncontrolled global pool
safe_units: independent destinations/OD batches with indexed ordered collection

simd.default: stable compiler auto-vectorization over contiguous SoA loops
simd.manual: runtime-detected std::arch kernels only after benchmark and parity
simd.portable_simd: not a stable default dependency; std::simd remains nightly-only
simd.external_crate: admit a stable SIMD crate only through a dedicated evidence-backed PR

priority: JAX typed FFI to custom CUDA
PyTorch custom operator only when tensor/training ecosystem is required
admission: no canonical state mutation split between CPU and GPU
explicit VRAM and failure fallback behavior
gpu.default: optional after Rust CPU engine parity; GPU work must not block Rust-default promotion

backend_policy.promotion: rust is default only after RUST-PR-014
backend_policy.after_promotion: Python oracle remains explicit debug/test backend, not silent fallback

architectural: one coarse Python-to-Rust step call per requested chunk
zero .tolist() calls in the Rust-default step path
no Python loop over links, turns, routes or agents in the default path
Python wall share below 5 percent during a no-UI step chunk, measured explicitly

promotion_targets.note: Engineering targets, not scientific claims; failure yields HOLD rather than threshold changes.
